segments.name: Cloudflare platform
segments.note: All of Cloudflare's revenue — its connectivity cloud platform for making websites, applications and networks faster and more secure. Cloudflare reports as a single operating segment, so this is the total revenue; up 39% YoY.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Selling the platform and winning customers; includes $63.178M of stock-based compensation and related payroll taxes, and $4.563M of amortization of acquired intangible assets.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building the platform and new products (R&D); includes $66.474M of stock-based compensation and related payroll taxes.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office (G&A); includes $39.754M of stock-based compensation and related payroll taxes and a $10.667M legal reserve and settlements charge.

opex.name: Restructuring and other charges
opex.note: Restructuring and other charges in the quarter; $161.711M for the first nine months of 2026.

oneTimers: Restructuring and other charges were $11.018M in Q3 ($161.711M in the first nine months) — excluded from Cloudflare's non-GAAP results.
A legal reserve and settlements charge of $10.667M sits inside general and administrative expense in Q3 — also excluded from non-GAAP results.

Stock-based compensation and related employer payroll taxes totaled $174.103M in Q3 across cost of revenue and operating expenses — the main reason GAAP shows a loss while non-GAAP operating income was $137.084M.
verdict: Cloudflare's revenue jumped 39% to $783M — its fastest growth in nearly four years — but stock pay, restructuring and legal charges left it with a $34M GAAP net loss despite $82M of free cash flow.
otherDetail: Interest income of $45.363M, less $3.545M of interest expense and $1.187M of other expense, net — total non-operating income of $40.631M.
footerNote: Cloudflare reports a single operating segment. GAAP loss from operations was $67.926M; non-GAAP income from operations was $137.084M after adding back stock-based compensation and other items listed in the release. Chart note: Cloudflare's running costs exceeded its gross profit; other income covered part of the gap, so the chart draws the remaining $34M net loss as a 'Covered by cash on hand' source, which also covers the $7M tax bill.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: basic and diluted, vs $0.00 a year ago

follow100Note: Sales and marketing alone takes $43.19 of every $100 Cloudflare takes in, and the quarter ends with a $4.35 loss per $100 of revenue. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Growth accelerated to a near-four-year high
takeaways.text: Revenue hit $782.5M, up 39% YoY. Management called it Cloudflare's best quarter ever and its fastest revenue growth in nearly four years, with current RPO up 37% YoY.

takeaways.title: GAAP operating loss widened
takeaways.text: GAAP loss from operations was $67.9M, or 8.7% of revenue, versus a $37.5M loss a year ago. Stock-based compensation of $174.1M sits inside the GAAP costs; excluding it and other items, non-GAAP operating income was $137.1M.

takeaways.title: Cash flow stayed positive despite the loss
takeaways.text: Net cash from operations was $215.4M and free cash flow (operations less equipment purchases and capitalized software) was $82.1M, or 10% of revenue. Cash, equivalents and available-for-sale securities were $5,128.7M at September 30.
